newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom says first half satisfactory.
newsitem.headline: Telecom says first half satisfactory.

text.p: Telecom Corporation of New Zealand said on Thursday its first half earnings to September were satisfactory, although the rate of growth had slowed, and it was positive about its outlook.
It posted net earnings of NZ$360.9 million for the first half of 1996/97, an increase of $22.9 million, or 6.8 percent, from the $338 million for the same period last year.
Net earnings for the second quarter of $183.8 million represented an increase of $5.1 million, or 2.9 percent, compared with the same quarter last year.

"Results for the first half, and for the second quarter of fiscal 1997 were satisfactory in view of New Zealand's reduced economic growth rate and the difficulties experienced by Pacific Star," Chief Executive Roderick Deane said.

He said Telecom continued to grow its volumes and revenues "in a manner reflecting the basic resilience of our business". Telecom announced it would begin a NZ$1 billion share repurchase programme soon after its third quarter result in February. That repurchase would be half on market and half via the combined 49.9 percent holdings held by Bell Atlantic and Ameritech.
Telecom's Australian unit, Pacific Star, lost NZ$22.5 million in the half year.
Telecom said it would pay a second quarter dividend of 9.5 cents per ordinary share in December 1996, up from 8.5 cents in the second quarter of last year.
Excluding the results from Pacific Star Group, net earnings increased by $37.1 million, or 10.7 percent, for the half year and $11.4 million, or 6.2 percent, for the second quarter.
Deane said telecommunications were being applied more broadly across all spheres of the economy.
"This is the key feature of our positive business outlook. Growing usage of ehhanced network services and the tremendous demand for our Xtra (Internet) online services point the way."
Revenue increased $124.7 million for the half year and $52.5 million for the second quarter.
Deane said Telecom continued to achieve growth in volumes and revenues significantly higher than growth in the general level of activity.
"Telecom's lower rate of revenue growth, compared with that of volumes, reflects market-driven price reductions and the effects of the slowing economy," he said.
He said he expected competition to remain intense, most notably in mobile phones where revenues fell in the second quarter.
Expenses for the half year incresed 9.5 percent, $92.9 million, reflecting the establishment of Xtra and cable TV system First Media.

Earnings from operations increased $31.8 million, 5.7 percent for the half year and 1.1 percent in the second quarter. Local calls revenues increased 5.2 percent in the half, and 4.2 percent in the second quarter.
National calls revenue grew 3.4 percent and 1.6 percent in the seond quarter.
International calls revenue grew by 3.5 percent in the half year and two percent in the second quarter.

Cellular and mobile services revenue grew 1.6 percent for the half year and decreased 5.1 percent in the second quarter. The lower growth reflected intensive competition pressure both on equipment prices and usage and the economic slowdown.
Enhanced network services revenue grew 44 percent in the half year and 45.3 percent in the second quarter.
Directories revenue grew 14 percent in the half year and 22 percent in the second quarter.
